turns.user: Hollow cylinder, 300 mm diameter, 500 mm tall, 20 mm nozzle, 10 mm layers, 20 s per layer. Fresh density 2150 kg/m3, static yield stress 1.2 kPa, Athix 0.5 Pa/s. Will it stand?
turns.text:
I’ll run the buildability calculation for the stated geometry and material properties, then report the physical verdict and limiting failure mode.
**No.** The buildability calculation predicts plastic collapse around layer 11, at roughly 107 mm, well short of the 500 mm target. With the calculator’s default safety factor of 1.5, the limit is about 7 layers. The empirical collapse probability is 87.7%, but the physical collapse check is the basis for the verdict.

At the stated 20 s per layer, the calculator estimates that reaching the target would require either an initial static yield stress of about **8.63 kPa** or an Athix of about **7.93 Pa/s**, with the other stated property held fixed. With the current material, its calculated minimum cycle time is **317 s per layer**. That schedule also needs an open-time check, since open time was not supplied.

The calculation assumed a 23.69 mm deposited width from the 20 mm nozzle. Buckling was not evaluated, so resolving plastic collapse alone would not establish that the cylinder will stand. Verify any revised mix and schedule by a print trial.
